newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Late talks scheduled to avert Colombian oil strike.
newsitem.headline: Late talks scheduled to avert Colombian oil strike.

text.p: Colombian oil workers leaders are scheduled to meet President Ernesto Samper and other senior ministers Tuesday night in a last minute bid to avert an all-out strike, union representatives said.

Members of the 7,000-strong USO oil union ratified a strike decision at an extraordinary assembly in the oil production center of Barracabermeja late Monday but leaders remained tight- lipped over precisely when the action would start.

"We will not publicize the zero hour for the start of the strike because the action is likely to be declared illegal and the government is likely to order in the armed forces," Gustavo Triana, a member of the USO national directorate, told Reuters.

He said the union would restate its demands when it met Samper, Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar, Interior Minister Horacio Serpa and newly-appointed Justice Minister Alma Beatriz Rengifo Tuesday.
The union and the state-run oil company Ecopetrol have been bogged down in collective contract talks since early January.

The union is protesting at Ecopetrol's plan to divide crude and gas operations, its refusal to employ 2,000 additional workers and at the arrest last December of about 10 USO officials on terrorism charges, link to a wave of dynamite attacks on oil pipelines.
Triana said the only way to avert a strike would be for the government to cede ground on the union's demands.

Wednesday is widely being tipped as the day on which a strike would start if Tuesday night's talks fail to yield any solution. Triana would not confirm any start start date. The oil workers have pledged to paralyze all Ecopetrol's production, refining, pumping and transport operations.

Two of Colombia's main foreign oil multinationals, British Petroleum Co Plc and the Occidental Petroleum Corp, admit the strike action could also partially affect their operations since the pipelines through which the crude from their fields is pumped are operated by Ecopetrol.
